Problem: Scarcity of public real-world SMS spam benchmarks for academic research
Method: Naive Bayes, SVM, k-NN, and Rule-based Classifiers with BoW
Dataset/Setting: UCI SMS Spam Collection (5,574 English messages; 4,827 ham, 747 spam)
Metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F-measure, False Discovery Rate
Main Findings: Linear SVM achieved top overall performance (97.64% accuracy); established UCI corpus as standard benchmark
Limitations: Evaluated only basic tokenization and BoW; did not investigate preprocessing sensitivity or cross-seed variability

Problem: Detection of spam and phishing across multi-lingual English and Arabic SMS texts
Method: Hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture combining spatial CNN filters and temporal LSTM cells
Dataset/Setting: English SMS (UCI) and Arabic SMS datasets; word embeddings
Main Findings: Hybrid CNN-LSTM achieved 98.37% accuracy on English SMS, outperforming standalone CNN and LSTM
Limitations: High computational overhead and latency; unsuitable for low-power edge mobile deployment

Problem: Manual feature engineering bottlenecks in traditional SMS spam filters
Method: Comparative evaluation of 7 Deep Learning architectures vs. 6 Shallow ML models
Dataset/Setting: UCI SMS Spam Collection (5,574 messages); Word2Vec and GloVe embeddings
Main Findings: CNN and LSTM models reached up to 99.44% accuracy, marginally surpassing SVM and Random Forest
Limitations: Large parameter footprint and training time; lack of systematic statistical significance testing

Problem: Severe class imbalance in mobile SMS spam classification datasets
Method: BiLSTM network evaluated with data resampling and cost-sensitive loss adjustments
Dataset/Setting: Indigenous and benchmark SMS corpora with severe minority spam ratio
Main Findings: BiLSTM coupled with minority augmentation improved spam recall from 78.4% to 94.2%
Limitations: Synthetic sample generation introduces out-of-vocabulary artifacts and risk of overfitting

Problem: Scarcity or absence of labeled spam instances in dynamic streaming mobile environments
Method: Semi-supervised One-Class SVM (OCSVM) trained exclusively on legitimate ham messages
Dataset/Setting: UCI SMS Spam Collection (747 spam, 4,827 ham)
Metrics: Accuracy, True Positive Rate, False Positive Rate
Main Findings: OCSVM achieved 98.0% accuracy learning exclusively from normal traffic, flagging spam as anomalies
Limitations: Sensitive to hyperparameter nu; false positive rate (~3.0%) is unacceptably high for consumer SMS delivery

Problem: Impact of lexical and semantic text representations on classifier effectiveness
Method: Comparative evaluation of Word2Vec, TF-IDF, and n-grams across ML classifiers
Main Findings: TF-IDF with n-grams consistently matched or exceeded dense Word2Vec embeddings for linear classifiers
Limitations: Did not evaluate impact of stopword filtering or punctuation stripping on domain-specific spam tokens

Problem: Comparative effectiveness between classical machine learning and neural architectures
Method: Empirical benchmarking of Naive Bayes, SVM, LSTM, and CNN
Main Findings: Linear SVM matched CNN performance (98.2% vs 98.4%) while requiring orders of magnitude less training time
Limitations: Evaluated on a single train-test split without seed variability or significance testing

Problem: High computational complexity of mobile-based real-time SMS filtering systems
Method: Multinomial Naive Bayes evaluated with lightweight lexical tokenization
Main Findings: Naive Bayes achieved 97.4% accuracy with near-zero latency, demonstrating feasibility on constrained devices
Limitations: Naive Bayes exhibits lower spam recall due to independence assumption on correlated spam phrases

Citation: Al Saidat, Yerima & Shaalan (2024) [Procedia Comp. Sci.]
Problem: Fragmented benchmarking methodologies and lack of unified taxonomy in SMS/smishing research
Method: Comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of NLP and ML techniques
Dataset/Setting: Synthesis of 85 peer-reviewed studies across standard benchmark corpora
Metrics: Taxonomy classification, comparative metric ranges, computational efficiency
Main Findings: Highlights that traditional linear models (SVM, LR) remain competitive with Transformers for non-obfuscated SMS
Limitations: Identifies critical research gap: pervasive inconsistency in preprocessing protocols and reporting standards

Problem: Balancing false alarm rates and recall in enterprise SMS traffic filtering
Method: Hybrid supervised-unsupervised clustering and classification pipeline
Main Findings: Achieved 97.0% accuracy, 98.0% specificity, and 96.0% sensitivity, reducing false positives
Limitations: Complex multi-stage pipeline increases deployment latency compared to direct linear models
